title: Standards, local codes and contract scope
audience: Cleaners, supervisors and office staff who receive site instructions that cite standards, codes or local requirements for kitchen exhaust work.
learningOutcomes: Identify the standards and codes that a site instruction cites, and their source and edition.
Explain that a course reference is a lead for specialist review, not a binding site rule.
Read the contract scope and record the adopted local requirements.

instruction.heading: Why the citation matters
instruction.body: A site instruction often names a standard, a code or a local requirement. The name sounds authoritative, and it is tempting to act on it without checking what it says, which edition applies or whether the site has adopted it. That shortcut causes three kinds of error. You may follow a superseded edition. You may apply a national text where a state has changed it. You may treat a general reference as a rule for the specific site. This lesson does not teach the content of any standard. It teaches you to identify the document, to check its status, to record what the site relies on, and to refer any doubt to the person who can decide. The reader of this lesson is not expected to interpret an engineering standard. Interpretation belongs to the competent person named in the contract.

instruction.heading: Reading the source and its edition
instruction.body: Each citation needs five pieces of information on the record: the document type (for example a standard, a code, a regulation, a council requirement, a contract clause or a manufacturer's instruction), its number or title, its edition or amendment, its date of issue, and where you obtained it. Standards are revised over time, and a revised edition can replace an earlier one. The course's research notes list two related Australian standards for kitchen exhaust fire systems, AS 1851 on routine service of fire protection systems and AS/NZS 1668.1 on a related installation topic. A local council, a fire authority or a state adoption may apply a different text.

instruction.heading: Course references are leads
instruction.body: Course material, including this course, can point you to a standard, a topic or a question. It is not the site's rule. A course note may give example numbers, such as a grease depth or a cleaning interval, to show how a record might look. Those numbers are illustrations. They are not legal thresholds and must not be quoted as the threshold at a site. A legal inspection interval, a safe grease level or a fire-compliance result is set by the owner, the regulator or the competent person for the site, and recorded in the site documents. When a course reference is useful, record it as a lead, note what question it raises, and send that question to the competent person for review.

instruction.heading: Contract scope and the adopted local requirements
instruction.body: The contract defines what the cleaner has agreed to do. Read it alongside the site instruction. Look for the scope, the exclusions, the standard of finish, the method limits, the products allowed, the access arrangements and any clause that adopts a named standard or local requirement. Record the adopted local requirements as the site has stated them, with the document reference. Where the contract and the site instruction disagree, or where a citation conflicts with another citation, do not decide the conflict yourself. Refer it to the contract owner, record the conflict and the referral, and hold the affected task until the owner confirms the position in writing. A contract can allocate work and set standards between the parties. Until that question is answered, treat the legal duty as still applying, and send the question to the competent person, not to the cleaner.

instruction.heading: Duties are shared, so the record is shared
instruction.body: Under the model work health and safety framework, a person conducting a business or undertaking has a primary duty to manage risks so far as is reasonably practicable, and where more than one party has a duty for the same risk, each keeps its own responsibility and must consult and coordinate with the others. Safe Work Australia's model code on biological hazards restates this shared-duty approach in its section on duty holders. For this lesson, the practical point is that the cleaner's record is one part of the wider site record. Send the citation, the conflict and the adopted requirement to the other duty holders in writing, so that the site does not rely on a single person's memory.

procedure: Identify each standard, code, regulation or local requirement cited in the site instruction or contract.
For each citation, record the document type, number or title, edition or amendment, issue date and where it was obtained.
Check with the contract owner or the competent person whether the edition cited is the current edition the site has adopted.
Treat any course reference or example figure as a lead for specialist review. Do not quote it as a site rule.
Read the contract scope, the exclusions and the adopted local requirements, and record them with the document reference.
Where two sources conflict, record both, hold the affected task, and refer the conflict to the contract owner in writing.
Send the recorded citations and the referral to the other duty holders named on the site, and keep a copy in the job file.

workedExamples.situation: A site instruction cites a standard, but the edition given is older than the edition the site manager says the site has adopted. The job is to clean and record the accessible surfaces of a hood.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do before you start, and what do you write down?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not follow the older edition by default, and do not assume the newer edition applies. Record both citations, the source of each, and the discrepancy. Ask the contract owner or the competent person to confirm in writing which edition the site has adopted. Keep the written answer in the job file. Hold the part of the work that depends on the edition, and continue only the parts that do not.

workedExamples.situation: A course note in your training pack says a grease layer above a set depth requires immediate cleaning. The site instruction does not mention a depth. The supervisor asks you to tell the client the hood 'fails' at that depth.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Can you pass on the depth as the site rule, and what is the correct response?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The course figure is an illustrative example, not a site rule or a legal threshold. Do not tell the client that the hood fails. Describe only what you observed, record it, and tell the supervisor that the depth question has been referred to the competent person for review. The competent person decides whether any threshold applies at the site.

equipmentAndPpe: Copies or links to each cited document, with the edition or amendment recorded.
Contract scope, exclusions and site instruction, kept together in the job file.
Citation record sheet with columns for document type, reference, edition, date issued and source.
Conflict and referral form, with space for the contract owner's written answer.
PPE as set by the site and the task risk assessment. Reading documents does not require specialist PPE, but the job itself may.

commonErrors.error: Following a superseded edition because it is the one printed in the site folder.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the edition, and check it against the adopted version with the competent person.

commonErrors.error: Quoting a course example figure as a legal or site threshold.
commonErrors.prevention: Label course figures as illustrations, and refer any threshold question to the competent person.

commonErrors.error: Resolving a conflict between the contract and the site instruction on your own.
commonErrors.prevention: Record both sources, hold the affected task, and refer the conflict to the contract owner in writing.

commonErrors.error: Assuming a national standard applies unchanged in every state and territory.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the state or territory adoption with the competent person before relying on it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson does not grant a licence, competency or fire-authority approval for commercial exhaust-system work.

Under the model WHS framework, duties for the same risk are shared between the parties involved, and each party must consult and coordinate with the others. This lesson does not confirm how any particular state applies the framework to kitchen exhaust work.

This lesson does not grant any licence, certificate, plant-safety approval or specialist authority, and completing it does not make a cleaner a specialist. Compliance with a standard for kitchen exhaust fire systems is a specialist matter.

qualityStandard: Every citation in the case study is recorded with type, reference, edition, date issued and source.
The course figure in the worked example is not quoted as a site rule, and the question is referred for review.
The contract and site instruction conflict in the case study is recorded, the affected work is held, and the referral is in writing.
documentationEvidence: Citation record with type, reference, edition, date issued, source.
Contract scope and adopted local requirements, with document references.
Conflict and referral record with the contract owner's written response.
Notice to other duty holders of the recorded citations and conflicts.
summary: Record every standard, code or local requirement cited, with its edition and source.
Treat course references and example figures as leads, not site rules.
Record the contract scope and the adopted requirements, and refer any conflict to the contract owner.
Share the record with the other duty holders so the site does not rely on one person's memory.

knowledgeChecks.question: A site instruction cites a standard in an edition older than the one the site says it uses. What is correct?
options: Follow the cited edition, because it is the one written in the instruction
Record both editions, and ask the competent person or contract owner to confirm which applies
Follow the newest edition you can find, without checking whether the site has adopted it

knowledgeChecks.question: What is a course reference in this lesson?
options: A binding site rule that must be followed without question
A lead for specialist review, which is not a binding site rule
A certificate that proves a site is compliant

knowledgeChecks.question: The contract and the site instruction describe different scopes for the same hood. What is correct?
options: Decide which one is cheaper and follow it for the whole job today
Refer the conflict to the contract owner in writing, and hold the affected work
Start the work using the broader of the two scopes to be safe for the owner
